lead.headline: Vance rules out Iran talks until attacks on shipping stop
lead.dek: Kuwait says it intercepted Iranian missiles and drones; Brent holds near $96 as Hormuz transits lag pre-war.
body: Vice President JD Vance said Thursday the United States will not negotiate with Iran until it stops shooting at commercial shipping, as a U.S. official said Iran's overnight strikes did not affect American facilities in Kuwait or elsewhere in the region. Kuwait's army said it intercepted the missiles and drones, and the United Arab Emirates said no attack on it took place.

Brent crude rose to $95.67 a barrel Friday, up 7.1% on the week, France 24 reported, while Lloyd's List Intelligence counted an average of 102 ship transits a day through the Strait of Hormuz last week, against more than 130 a day before the war, CBS News reported. AAA said U.S. diesel reached a record $5.85 a gallon and regular gasoline averaged $4.14.

Vance said he would not call the six-month conflict a war because "right now, there is no active shooting," and said the U.S. is investigating but is "extremely skeptical" of Iranian reports that a U.S. strike hit a wedding in Kuhestak. South Korea said it is reviewing contributions to Hormuz security, France 24 reported, and Iran's first vice president said any answer to a future U.S. attack would be "asymmetric."

art.caption: Three working vessels ride at anchor off Bandar Abbas in the Strait of Hormuz, where transits run a fifth below pre-war levels.

briefs.headline: Missouri Supreme Court blocks the Trump-backed House map
briefs.summary: The court unanimously ruled Thursday that a referendum petition with nearly 300,000 signatures was valid, restoring the prior districts for November; the attorney general said she will appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court.

briefs.headline: Justice Department asks the Supreme Court to revive the mail-ballot rule
briefs.summary: Judge Talwani has not ruled on an injunction; the Postal Service told her its ballot portal will be usable "sometime next week," and Justice Jackson set responses to the government's application for Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Treasury moves to end tax breaks for schools that use race
briefs.summary: Proposed IRS rules would deny 501(c)(3) status to private schools with race-based admissions or aid from tax years beginning after May 31, 2027; Treasury said as many as 18,000 schools could be affected.

briefs.headline: Feminist pioneer Gloria Steinem dies at 92
briefs.summary: The Ms. magazine co-founder died Wednesday at her home in New York City, her foundation said; no cause was given. A memoir was due this fall.

briefs.headline: Nepal's toll reaches 1,287 as two are pulled alive from a tunnel
briefs.summary: Two Trishuli 3A hydropower workers were rescued after nine days underground; the disaster authority counted 1,287 dead and about 5,083 missing by Friday noon, a figure that now includes unidentified bodies.

briefs.headline: Pacific leaders ask for 24 hours' notice of missile tests
briefs.summary: The forum's Palau communique called on states testing intercontinental missiles to give at least a day's notice after July's Chinese launch toward Tuvalu; Nauru's dissent was recorded in the text.

briefs.headline: Volkswagen to cut another 50,000 jobs worldwide
briefs.summary: The supervisory board approved a plan Friday doubling planned cuts to 100,000, with the Emden, Zwickau, Neckarsulm and Hannover plants to be phased out from 2031, the company said.

briefs.headline: Uber pulls out of Nigeria and Uganda immediately
briefs.summary: The company ended ride-hailing in both markets Thursday, citing costs and competition, and will keep operating in Egypt, Ghana, Kenya and South Africa; its help center stays open to Sept. 23.

briefs.headline: Morrisey announces a $12B data center for Mason County
briefs.summary: Starwood Digital Ventures received state high-impact certification for a campus at West Columbia near Point Pleasant, the governor said Thursday; the company put it at 300 permanent jobs.

briefs.headline: Justice Wooton returns to work after dehydration treatment
briefs.summary: The Supreme Court justice was treated at CAMC Memorial and released Wednesday evening, then was back at the Capitol Thursday morning, the court said; Wednesday's canceled arguments will be rescheduled.

briefs.headline: Brooke High principal jailed over cameras in girls' locker rooms
briefs.summary: Eric James, 53, faces an interception count and two breaking-and-entering counts after deputies found cameras in a locker room and a dance dressing room, Sheriff Richard Beatty said; bail is $100,000 cash.

briefs.headline: Vape shop owners sue over the state's new Vape Safety Act
briefs.summary: Three operators of about 30 shops and a manufacturer filed in federal court in Charleston, arguing the law's citizenship requirement and product rules violate the First, Fifth and 14th Amendments.

regional.item: Cabell County EMS opened a grant-funded simulation lab with manikins that mimic vital signs and smoke inhalation, with an open house planned for October.
Kanawha County takes applications through Sept. 30 for a $2M USDA flood buyout covering Campbells Creek, Cabin Creek and Cross Lanes.
The Pond Creek Bridge on WV 68 partially reopened Thursday, one lane by day and two at night; the DOH expects it finished Sept. 12, nearly a month late.
The Summers County Sheriff's Office swore in two new deputies and an animal control officer Wednesday before Judge Mann.

away.item: The National Science Foundation this week awarded $7.9M over four years to a Bennington College-led PFAS research network, $4.8M of it to the college itself.

hotspots.item: The Lilly Mountaineers play the Jerry Run Summer Theater at Cleveland on Saturday, Sept. 5, at 7 p.m., $10 at the door, on the county's events calendar.
Novant Health and Pender Memorial filed Thursday for state approval of a $15M freestanding emergency department in Hampstead, to open by June 2029.

briefs.headline: Eby breaks ground in Prince George on the North Coast power line
briefs.summary: The premier and federal minister Tim Hodgson marked the start Thursday of the Prince George-Terrace line, backed by $3.9B in federal and provincial money; the first 165 km to Glenannan is due by mid-2030.

briefs.headline: Eby says the NDP will not court B.C. Conservative defectors
briefs.summary: The premier cited a "fairly significant gap" on U.S. relations, First Nations and human rights between his party and the nine MLAs who have quit Findlay's caucus since mid-August.

briefs.headline: Court extends the Walbran blockade injunction to 2028
briefs.summary: B.C. Supreme Court Justice H. William Veenstra extended Tsawak-Qin Forestry's injunction to Jan. 31, 2028, citing several hundred spiked trees in its cutblocks and a risk of injury or death to fallers.

briefs.headline: Ford's PCs and the NDP hold their seats in Ontario byelections
briefs.summary: PC Jeff Beattie won Hamilton East-Stoney Creek with 39%, Susan Lahey held York-Simcoe and New Democrat Fatima Shaban kept Scarborough Southwest on Thursday; turnout was just over 25%.

briefs.headline: Ottawa orders 313 Canadian-built Via Rail cars for $4.7B
briefs.summary: Carney said in Thunder Bay that Alstom will build the fleet in Canada, the first domestic Via car production in 40 years, supporting 700 jobs in Ontario and Quebec; no delivery date was given.

briefs.headline: ISRO launches its first geosynchronous imaging satellite
briefs.summary: A GSLV-F17 lifted off from Sriharikota at 2:55 a.m. IST Friday carrying the 2,367-kg EOS-05, the agency's first launch since a PSLV failed in January; the satellite reached a 171-by-31,026-km transfer orbit.

briefs.headline: BepiColombo sheds its transfer module on approach to Mercury
briefs.summary: ESA said the Mercury Transfer Module separated from the ESA and JAXA orbiters Thursday, 200 million km from Earth, with all systems nominal; orbit insertion is set for Nov. 21.

briefs.headline: Pig kidney kept a patient off dialysis for 271 days, study says
briefs.summary: Mass General Brigham reports in The Lancet that a 66-year-old man lived 271 days on a gene-edited pig kidney before receiving a human kidney in January, the longest such course reported.

briefs.headline: Nagoya team builds a nanoribbon that switches its twist
briefs.summary: Chemists report in Nature Communications a graphene nanoribbon whose helical twist flips direction when the solvent is changed to beta-pinene, and holds only while in that solvent.

briefs.headline: Nvidia confirms a $12.9B deal for Hugging Face
briefs.summary: CEO Jensen Huang said the model-hosting site, with 3 million models and 18 million developers, will stay open and will not require Nvidia chips; Hugging Face turned down a $500M offer from Nvidia last year.

briefs.headline: Study finds AI-written text in 15% of UK parliamentary statements
briefs.summary: Chalmers University and Edinburgh Napier researchers analyzed 17,774 UK and Swedish parliamentary texts from 2021 to April 2026 and found none disclosed AI use, Euronews reported; the UK share was 3.5% in 2022.

briefs.headline: KAIST tool repairs up to 87% of faulty AI-written database queries
briefs.summary: SafeQL fixed execution errors in as many as 87.4% of flawed SQL queries on the BIRD benchmark and cut token use up to 15-fold, the university reports in a paper at this week's VLDB conference in Boston.

kicker: Sports & Sportsman has Hoshoryu at the council's practice, the Pirates' series win and Saturday's three college openers.
